title:
Namespace type for the faulty sensor module in the reliability app. In the following documentation, you will find
a general overview of what this module is, some high level implementation details, and a list of types, functions,
and fields to read. The more granular the documentation (e.g. function docs), the more specific and accurate it will
be. This is a complex feature and copying all the details in once place (this type) would cause a lot of redundancy.

The purpose of this module is that sometimes [sensors](Sensor) become faulty or have routine maintenance.
Over the duration of this downtime, models that use the sensor as input will likely perform sub-optimally.
This module provides both a method of marking sensors as faulty, and a way to automatically adjust models to account
for the faulty sensor.

**Steps in the faulty sensor process:**
- Sensor(s) are marked as `faulty` or `operational` by a user.
  - Details at: {@link Sensor#operationalStatus} + {@link SensorOperationalStatusTimedValue} +
      {@link SensorOperationalStatusEnum#FAULTY}
- Identify the list of model/asset relations that are using the updated sensors as features or masks.
  - Details at:
    - {@link FaultySensor.ModelImpactMapReduceJob} - General docs
    - {@link FaultySensor.ModelImpactMapReduceJob#filterRelationsImpactedBySensorsBatch}
- Validate which of the affected models can be retrained.
  - Overview:
    - If the sensor is used in a mask, the model cannot be retrained.
    - If the resulting model without the sensor will have no features, the model cannot be retrained.
    - If the model contains features that is not parsable to understand the sensors used, the model cannot be
      retrained.
  - Details at:
    - {@link FaultySensor.ModelImpactMapReduceJob#doValidateModelWithDatasetPrepCanBeRetrained}
    - {@link FaultySensor.ModelRetrainValidationErrorEnum}
- Retrain the models that can be retrained.
  - Overview:
    - For the model that should be retrained, identify the model's original (called source of truth) model.
       - Details at: {@link FaultySensor.RiskModelSourceOfTruthRelation}
    - Remove all features that use a sensor in the faulty status.
    - Retrain the model on the same time period as the original model.
    - Deploy the new model.
  - Details at:
    - {@link FaultySensor.Orchestrator.Spec.Process}
    - {@link FaultySensor.Orchestrator.Spec.Retrain}
- Provide notifications to the user about all retraining successes or failures.
  - Overview:
    - Users are notified if a model was not retrained because it failed validation.
      - Details at: {@link FaultySensor.Notification#createNotificationsFromMapReduceResult}
    - Users are notified about successful model retraining or failures during the retraining process.
      - Details at: {@link FaultySensor.Notification#createNotificationsFromModelRetraining}
  - Details at:
    - {@link FaultySensor.Notification}
- Automatically return sensors to operational status based on the user specified end date.
    - Details at:
       - {@link SensorOperationalStatusTimedValue#endDate}
       - {@link Sensor#updateExpiredFaultySensors}

The previous steps are all orchestrated by the {@link FaultySensor.Orchestrator} type. This is another great entry
point to understand how the pieces all fit together.

You can find more details on this process in the inner types that implement this module.
name: FaultySensor
